source.title: Tiny Mech Interp Projects: Emergent Positional Embeddings of Words

record.file_problem: None; the full post text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The post discusses the IOI circuit as motivation but probes word-index information in GPT-2 Small; it does not test IOI behavior or the circuit versions.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern decoding which of seven random words a token belongs to, not IOI performance or the IOI circuit. The post also mentions a proposed IOI-related hypothesis, but reports no test of it.
record.test_reason: The post cites the IOI circuit finding as motivation and reports only a layer-3 linear probe of word index on random-word prompts in GPT-2 Small. It runs no IOI prompts, no circuit analysis and no ablations, so its results bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The author tentatively concludes that GPT-2 Small linearly represents word index beyond absolute position, most clearly for early words. He stresses that the experiment is rough, may be confounded by absolute position and space-prefixed tokens, and does not show the model uses these representations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a layer-3 logistic-regression probe to decode word index from GPT-2 Small residuals; it does not identify or intervene on an IOI circuit.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe performance is reported as weaker for later words; the post also notes unbalanced absolute positions and a fixed prefix as limitations.

fits_no_version.finding: A logistic-regression probe on the layer-3 residual stream of GPT-2 Small decodes which of seven random words a token ends. Decoding is clear for early words, even at a fixed absolute position, and weaker for later words. No accuracy is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPT-2 Small represents emergent word-level positional information (word index), linearly decodable from its early-layer residual stream; this is the author's proposed basis for position signals in IOI.

record.problems: The author reports no numerical probe accuracy and relies on visual inspection. Absolute position was not balanced, the prefix was fixed, only layer 3 was examined, and the probe may exploit tokens beginning with a space. The author did not test whether the decoded directions are used by the model.

untested.parts: Untested: the 26 heads, the 7 head classes, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
Untested: name-mover ablation and backup heads.
Untested: other models, sizes, checkpoints, and reuse for other tasks.
Untested: alternative circuit-finding methods, ablation types and metrics.
Untested: how ablation, metric and prompt distribution affect faithfulness and completeness.
Untested: name orders, templates and more names. The post only restates the original paper's cross-template patching observation and runs no test of it.

record.verdict_notes: The link to IOI is only motivational: the post cites the original paper's observation that position signals can be patched across templates, which bears on V6. The post itself runs no IOI test, so it gets no verdict on any version.

versions.untested_parts: The IOI circuit's heads, roles, faithfulness, completeness, and minimality are not tested.
No name-mover ablation or self-repair test.
No IOI circuit comparisons across models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks.
No comparison of circuit-finding methods, ablations, or IOI metrics.
No evaluation of IOI circuit faithfulness or completeness under differing methods, metrics, or prompt distributions.
No IOI tests across name orders, templates, or numbers of names.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Trained logistic regression on layer-3 residuals to predict the word index of each word's last token.

conditions.value: early words; the post highlights word two versus word three
fixed 19-token prefix followed by seven random lowercase English words

rows.measure: Qualitative probe performance for predicting word index at a given absolute position
rows.value: The post says the probe distinguishes early word indices clearly even at the same absolute position; it does not report an accuracy.
rows.note: The author describes the result by visual inspection and says the numerical probe accuracy was not recorded. Absolute position was not balanced.
rows.check: The row measures word-index probe decoding, not IOI. No accuracy or baseline is reported; the description comes from eyeballing a plot. 'observed' does not apply to any claim version.

rows.measure: Qualitative probe performance for predicting word index at a given absolute position
rows.value: Performance is described as much worse and messier for later words, but still visibly better than random.

rows.check: Same as R1: a qualitative probe result on word index for later words, unrelated to any IOI version. No numbers are given.
